notes:
Account summary
- Existing Dedicated customer (renewed FY25). Runs Dedicated in VPC (us-east-1 primary; eu-west-1 standby for EU workloads).
- Workloads: (1) real-time agent assist + summarization for internal ops, (2) embeddings for KB/doc-search, (3) periodic batch re-indexing.
- Theme: predictable baseline traffic + sharp, scheduled spikes (Fri afternoons + month-end reconciliation).

Current footprint (as of last check-in)
- Dedicated tenant: NBP-prod-dedicated
- Regions: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (limited EU-only routes)
- Models: mix of chat + embedding endpoints; they pin versions tightly and are sensitive to unexpected fallbacks.
- Their ops team monitors p95/p99 latency + error rate; they page internally on >2% 5xx over 5m.

Why burst capacity / what changed
- They have a weekly batch surge that can 3–6x normal QPS for ~30–90 minutes. Historically they over-provisioned baseline GPUs to avoid throttling.
- Quote from 6/18 deep dive: "I don’t need more steady-state. I need a guaranteed escape hatch for the Friday spike without paying for it all week."
- They are willing to accept occasional burst denial, but want: deterministic limits, clear deny reasons, and predictable fallback behavior.

Historical incidents / health notes
- 2025-02: Scaling friction when they increased concurrency quickly; saw intermittent 429s and queuing. Root cause likely client-side retry storm + tenant concurrency cap. Mitigation: tuned retry + tightened per-route limits.
- 2025-04 (SUP-3198): Reported throttling during predictable spike window. They asked for a "temporary headroom" mechanism rather than permanent capacity add.
- 2025-06 pilot prep: During Redwood internal load test in us-east burst pool, they experienced mild p99 drift on one route (customer noticed in their dashboards). Follow-up ticket logged (SUP-3221). No data exposure concerns raised; mostly latency jitter + confusion about whether to retry.
- 2025-07 (SUP-3277): Confusion around burst-denied semantics. They want guidance: when to retry vs fail fast; requested headers to explain deny reason without leaking internal pool details.

Burst beta enrollment (planned)
- Target: enroll as design-partner/pilot customer for Dedicated Burst Capacity (private beta) in us-east-1.
- Terms: shadow metering in pilot; they want at least a monthly report attributing baseline vs burst tokens/requests.
- Guardrails they requested (must-have):
  - Max burst concurrency cap (hard)
  - Max burst tokens/sec (hard) + cooldown/backoff when denied
  - Optional allowlist of routes eligible for burst (they do NOT want embeddings to steal burst from real-time chat)
  - Time window preference (Fri 12:00–18:00 ET) — OK if it’s advisory in v1.
- Acceptable degradation modes (from calls):
  - OK: burst denied with explicit reason + retry-after
  - OK: fallback to baseline (queue) if latency < agreed SLO
  - NOT OK: silent region failover that violates data residency (EU data must stay EU)

Technical requirements snapshot
- Latency targets (chat): p95 < 800ms, p99 < 2.5s during baseline; during burst they accept p99 up to ~3.5s but need <1% 5xx.
- Throughput target during spikes: sustain ~4x baseline for 60 minutes (they estimate 2.5–3M tokens/min at peak, but number varies by prompt size).
- Routing/fallback expectations:
  - Prefer baseline tenant first.
  - If bursting, only within same region (no cross-region burst for residency).
  - If burst denied, return explicit error (and do not “helpfully” route to hosted fleet).

Security/compliance notes
- Requires SSO/SAML for console access + role-based access controls.
- Audit logs required for any burst config changes (who/what/when), and they asked specifically about “who enabled burst” and “who changed limits.”
- Data residency: EU routes must remain EU. They asked if burst pools share clusters with hosted; answer must be: isolated capacity with strict noisy-neighbor protections; no data commingling at app layer.
- KMS: customer-managed keys for stored artifacts; for inference they focus on network isolation + logs retention.

Activity timeline (recent)

Open questions to resolve before enablement

- Confirm initial limit proposal (starting conservative): burst concurrency + burst TPS and cooldown parameters.
- Confirm which dashboards the customer will get (at minimum: burst usage, burst deny rate, and latency during burst window).
